title: A swing in time
question: What makes a pendulum return sooner—or later?
description: Release a physical pendulum, change its length and gravity, and compare what you observe with the small-angle prediction.
imageAlt: Original geometric teaching diagram for A swing in time

title: The camera, opened up
question: How does scattered light become a focused picture?
description: Take apart a schematic camera, follow light through an ideal lens and discover why an image can be real, virtual or impossible to catch on a nearby screen.
imageAlt: Original geometric teaching diagram for The camera, opened up

title: The Great Wave, made by hand
question: How many kinds of work live inside one famous image?
description: Look past an icon. Inspect boats, mountain and blue; follow the hands that turned a design into a printed sheet, then compare two other views of Fuji.
imageAlt: The Great Wave, made by hand — historical collection image
scope: Edo-period Japanese printmaking and the Fuji series

title: When light learned to stay
question: How did a passing view become something we could keep?
description: Explore the invention of photography through early photographs and the choices behind them: fixing light, making copies, composing a scene and deciding what an image can prove.
imageAlt: A salted paper print of an open wooden door, a leaning broom, stonework and a hanging lantern.
scope: Early photography in France and Britain

title: Pompeii, beyond the ash
question: What can a buried city really tell us about the people who lived there?
description: Explore a city through work, volcanic deposits and the evidence of later observers. Inspect historical views and discover why Pompeii is more than a day frozen in time.
imageAlt: An albumen photograph of an excavated Pompeian street in the 1860s, with raised crossing stones and exposed building fronts.
scope: Pompeii and the Bay of Naples; later records and research

title: Shape a sound
question: Why can the same note have a different character?
description: Build a tone from four harmonics, see the resulting waveform and listen deliberately. The same explanation remains available without audio.

title: The shape of a signal
question: How does a movement of one hand cross an ocean?
description: Start with a real telegraph key. Follow the code, people and precarious ocean connection that turned a contact into a network.
imageAlt: The shape of a signal — historical collection image
scope: Washington, Baltimore and the North Atlantic

title: Signals and decisions
question: How can simple rules produce a useful decision?
